1.why: Server-side authorization checks that MFA settings belong to the signed-in user via session.accountId.

2.why: Verification codes are single-use (preAuthSessions.used flag) and not reusable across users.

3.why: Previous sessions are not invalidated when MFA is enabled; only new sessions are created.

4.why: OTP shared secret and backup codes are stored encrypted (AES-GCM) and hashed (HMAC-SHA256), respectively.

5.why: Secrets and codes are generated using crypto.getRandomValues (cryptographically secure RNG).

6.why: Secrets, OTPs, and session tokens are kept out of browser storage and non-HttpOnly cookies (only HttpOnly cookies used).

7.why: Server-side input validation is performed for email, phone, OTP, and recovery codes (e.g., validEmail, validOtp).

8.why: Contextual output encoding is applied via TextEncoder/JSON.stringify, and CSP nonce prevents script execution.

9.why: No open redirects; all navigation is client-side or to hardcoded internal paths.

10.why: Secure headers (CSP, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options) are set on every response.

11.why: Session cookies are set with HttpOnly, Secure, and SameSite=Strict attributes.

12.why: In TEST_MODE, mock identity codes are logged to the browser console and Logs panel (violates requirement).

13.why: Verification codes (preAuthSessions) are single-use (used flag) and time-bound (expiresAt).

14.why: Failed verification attempts are rate-limited (MAX_FAILURES=5) and locked out (LOCK_MS=10 minutes).

15.why: Session identifier is rotated on authentication, but idle/absolute timeouts are enforced without explicit invalidation on logout (though logout deletes the session).
